card.title: Rebuild a Tree From Two Walks
card.sub: Divide and Conquer + Index Map · Medium

a1.cap: preorder (node, left, right) and inorder (left, node, right) are two traversals of the same tree with distinct values. Rebuild the tree and return its root.

lines: preorder (node, left, right) and inorder (left, node, right) are two traversals of the same tree with distinct values. Rebuild the tree and return its root.

a1.cap: For example, with preorder = [3,9,20,15,7], inorder = [9,3,15,20,7], the answer is [3,9,20,null,null,15,7].
a1.say: For example, with preorder equals 3, 9, 20, 15, 7, inorder equals 9, 3, 15, 20, 7, the answer is 3, 9, 20, null, null, 15, 7.

a1.cap: Preorder lists each root before its subtrees, so we can take roots from it one by one. A root's position in the inorder list splits the remaining values into its left part and right part.
A hash map from value to inorder index makes each split instant.
Let's walk through it with preorder = [3,9,20,15,7], inorder = [9,3,15,20,7].
a1.say: Let's walk through it with preorder equals 3, 9, 20, 15, 7, inorder equals 9, 3, 15, 20, 7.

a1.cap: 3 is the next root. In the in-order list it splits positions 0 to 4.
9 is the next root. In the in-order list it splits positions 0 to 0.
20 is the next root. In the in-order list it splits positions 2 to 4.
15 is the next root. In the in-order list it splits positions 2 to 2.
7 is the next root. In the in-order list it splits positions 4 to 4.
Time complexity is O(n) and extra space is O(n).
a1.say: Time complexity is O of n and extra space is O of n.

a1.cap: That's the Divide and Conquer + Index Map approach. Now try writing it yourself, in Java or Python!
a1.say: That's the Divide and Conquer plus Index Map approach. Now try writing it yourself, in Java or Python!
